facts.claim: There is no special 'Air Force One salary'; the pilots are commissioned officers assigned to the 89th Airlift Wing, paid by military rank and years of service.
Lieutenant colonels with under two years of service earn $7,295 per month in base pay and those with six years of aviation service $9,250; colonels earn $8,751 and $10,284 respectively.

A lieutenant colonel flying the presidential aircraft in 2026 can expect total compensation of $200,000-$250,000 (base around $130,000-$145,000, housing allowance around $30,000-$45,000, retention bonus around $35,000-$50,000); a colonel can expect $235,000-$285,000.
Training a fast-jet pilot costs around $10-15 million, and commercial airlines can offer roughly double the total compensation of the Air Force.
Senior widebody captains at Delta, American and United routinely earn $400,000 to over $520,000 a year, with top hourly rates around $465 per hour.

The 89th Airlift Wing is based at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland; its fleet includes two VC-25A aircraft, one VC-25B 'Bridge', four C-32A, four C-40B and eleven C-37A/B aircraft, with a ready force of over 1,800 personnel.

Air Force pilots can retire after 20 years with an immediate lifetime pension, often in their late 30s or early 40s; the Big Three contribute around 18% of pay into 401(k)-type plans and their pilots generally fly to the FAA mandatory retirement age of 65.

zh.title: 空軍一號飛行員年薪約21.5萬美元？美軍薪給對比三大航寬體機長
zh.summary: 空軍一號沒有專屬薪給：執飛總統專機的美國空軍軍官依軍階與年資支薪，中校總薪酬約20萬至25萬美元、上校約23.5萬至28.5萬美元；相較之下，達美、美國與聯合航空的資深寬體機長年薪可達40萬至52萬美元以上。
body: 空軍一號飛行員年薪約21.5萬美元、三大航寬體機長可逾48萬美元的說法，大致符合實際數字，但背後的支薪邏輯完全不同。執飛總統專機的飛行員沒有專屬的「空軍一號薪給」：他們是派駐美國空軍第89空運聯隊的現役軍官，依軍階與年資支薪，與其他軍種同階軍官的基本薪給相同，不因所飛機型的尊榮程度而加給。培養一名戰機飛行員約需1,000萬至1,500萬美元，航空公司能開出約兩倍的總薪酬，使空軍面臨激烈的人才競爭。

依美軍薪給表，中校未滿兩年年資者月基本薪給為7,295美元、具6年飛行年資者為9,250美元；上校未滿兩年年資者8,751美元、6年飛行年資者10,284美元。但空軍一號飛行員實際年資遠高於此：中校通常具15至17年任官年資、上校21至24年。2026年執飛總統專機的中校，基本薪給約13萬至14.5萬美元，另加住房津貼約3萬至4.5萬美元、航空留任獎金約3.5萬至5萬美元與其他福利，總薪酬約20萬至25萬美元；上校總薪酬約23.5萬至28.5萬美元。總統專機飛行員多為中校（O-5）或上校（O-6），較實際執行作戰任務的戰機飛行員（多為中尉與上尉）資深；第89空運聯隊駐紮馬里蘭州安德魯斯聯合基地，負責總統、副總統與高層官員的專機任務。

民航方面則不受軍方薪給限制。達美、美國與聯合航空的資深寬體機長年薪通常為40萬至52萬美元以上，三家航空的頂級寬體機長時薪約465美元。民航機師同樣依年資與職級支薪，寬體機長薪資較高，主因是資深機師按年資競標寬體航線；機隊規模上，美國航空寬體機隊最小、最單純，計67架777與70架787，達美航空有57架767（逐步退役）、81架A330與41架A350，聯合航空則擁有88架787、96架777與53架767，為三家之最。比較時還須計入退休制度：空軍飛行員服役滿20年即可退役、於30多歲或40出頭開始領取終身俸；三大航新進機師傳統退休金大多已取消，改由公司提撥約18%薪資至401（k）型計畫，民航機師則一般飛至美國聯邦航空總署規定的65歲強制退休年齡。

en.title: Do Air Force One pilots earn around $215K while Big Three widebody captains clear $480K?
en.summary: There is no special Air Force One salary: the US Air Force officers who fly the presidential aircraft are paid by rank and years of service, with lieutenant colonels earning roughly $200,000–$250,000 in total compensation and colonels $235,000–$285,000 — while senior widebody captains at Delta, American and United can earn $400,000 to more than $520,000 a year.
body: The claim that Air Force One pilots earn around $215,000 while Big Three widebody captains clear $480,000 is broadly in line with the figures — but the two pay systems work entirely differently. The Air Force does not pay a special "Air Force One salary." The pilots who fly the presidential aircraft are commissioned officers assigned to the 89th Airlift Wing, paid according to military rank and years of service, with the same base pay as any other US officer of the same rank — it does not change with the prestige of the aircraft. That leaves the Air Force exposed: it can cost around $10–15 million to train a fast-jet pilot, and commercial airlines can offer roughly double the total compensation, sometimes with a better work-life balance.

Under the US military pay table, lieutenant colonels with less than two years of service earn $7,295 per month in base salary, while those with six years of aviation service earn $9,250 monthly; for colonels the figures are $8,751 and $10,284. In practice, Air Force One pilots have far longer service: lieutenant colonels typically have 15–17 years of commissioned service and colonels 21–24 years. A lieutenant colonel flying the presidential aircraft in 2026 can expect base pay of around $130,000 to $145,000, plus a Basic Allowance for Housing of around $30,000 to $45,000 and an Aviation Retention Bonus of around $35,000 to $50,000, plus other benefits, for total compensation of between $200,000 and $250,000; a colonel can expect $235,000 to $285,000. Presidential-airlift pilots are typically lieutenant colonels (O-5) or colonels (O-6), more senior than the first lieutenants (O-2) and captains (O-3) who typically fly fighter jets on combat missions. The 89th Airlift Wing is based at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, and operates the Air Force's primary executive and special air mission fleet.

Commercial operators face no such constraint. Senior widebody captains at Delta Air Lines, American Airlines and United Airlines routinely earn $400,000 to over $520,000 annually, with top hourly rates at all three carriers around $465 per hour. Commercial pilots are likewise paid on seniority and years of service, and widebody captains earn more mainly because senior pilots bid to fly widebody aircraft. American has the smallest and simplest widebody fleet of the three, with 67 Boeing 777s and 70 Boeing 787s; Delta has 57 legacy Boeing 767s being phased down, 81 Airbus A330s and 41 Airbus A350s; United has the largest, with 88 Boeing 787s, 96 Boeing 777s and 53 aging 767s. Pensions complicate the comparison: Air Force pilots are guaranteed a government-backed lifetime pension after 20 years of service and can retire in their late 30s or early 40s, while traditional pensions are largely gone for new hires at the Big Three, which contribute around 18% of pay into 401(k)-type plans, and commercial pilots generally fly until the FAA's mandatory retirement age of 65.
